summary: Increment 2 of the world-engine history program (MULTIPLY): thread the real per-body D-vector (D14 massGravity, D2 volatileFraction, D12 tidalHeating) through route()->writeBodyRelief->writePlateUpliftSphere via a NEW body-driver channel (separate from the grain-bake grainDrivers bundle), and build a calibrated driversToTune(D) in plates.js that makes PLATE_COUNT / UPLIFT_GAIN / CONTINENTAL_FRACTION respond to those drivers. Calibrated against a named D_earth constant so driversToTune(D_earth) returns a falsy/empty override and the Earth reference point is byte-identical to the validated plate POC. (D16 age was scoped then DESCOPED at Max's UAT 2026-06-28 — a static age nudge misrepresents age/history; its real home is the epoch model #6 + weathering #7. driversToTune accepts but ignores age.) Lab-only; never touches the despun/shell path, the grain bake, or game Planet.js.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: DETERMINISM + NO-RNG + BOUNDED: driversToTune is a pure function and the driver threading adds no RNG; writePlateUpliftSphere(carrier, D, {macroSeed, tune:driversToTune(D)}) run twice on the same fresh carrier yields byte-identical fields for every (seed x driver-combo); |U| < U_BOUND.

verifyVia.input: Static-grep the new driversToTune + threading code for /Math\.random\s*\(|Date\.now\s*\(/ (zero matches); run writePlateUpliftSphere with tune:driversToTune(D) twice for a grid of D-vectors x macroSeeds in {1,2,7,42}.
verifyVia.observable: Zero RNG matches; byte-identical U + plateDiag arrays (Float32/Int equality) across the two runs for every case; |U[i]| < U_BOUND for all nodes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: EARTH BYTE-IDENTITY (the load-bearing identity guard): with D_earth defined as a named constant and every transfer function calibrated to it, driversToTune(D_earth) returns a falsy/empty override so the `tune ? {...DEFAULTS, ...tune} : DEFAULTS` ternary takes the untouched DEFAULTS branch, and the plate field at the Earth reference point is byte-identical to a pre-change DEFAULTS-only baseline.

verifyVia.input: Capture a pre-change baseline U from writePlateUpliftSphere(carrier, {}, {macroSeed:s}) for s in {1,2,7,42}; then call driversToTune(D_earth) and writePlateUpliftSphere(carrier, D_earth, {macroSeed:s, tune:driversToTune(D_earth)}) for the same seeds.
verifyVia.observable: driversToTune(D_earth) is null or {} (empty) so the ternary selects DEFAULTS; U is byte-identical to the baseline for every seed; the existing plate AC2 structure test (boundary-organized, beats latitude) still passes unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: MONOTONE, CORRECT-SIGN DRIVER RESPONSE: each threaded driver (D14, D2, D12), swept across its range with the others held at the Earth point, moves its mapped plate parameter monotonically in ONE documented direction whose sign matches a cited physical rationale; off the Earth point the field measurably differs from the Earth baseline.

verifyVia.input: For each driver, sweep it across its calibrated range (others = D_earth) and build the field at each step; read the mapped parameter (plateCount, effective UPLIFT_GAIN / relief amplitude, continental area fraction) + corr(U, single-driver step index).
verifyVia.observable: Each driver's mapped parameter is monotone in its documented direction across the sweep (e.g. gravity up -> relief amplitude down; volatiles up -> continental fraction down; tidal heating up -> plate count up); the documented direction + rationale are recorded in the build note; |corr| measurably > 0 (field differs from the Earth baseline at the sweep extremes).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: NO-CLOBBER of the grain bake + sibling relief paths: the plate driver-response uses a NEW body-driver channel distinct from the grainDrivers bundle, so the grain-cube bake, the despun/ice-shell relief paths, and the ocean/drainage outputs are all byte-identical to a pre-change baseline.

verifyVia.input: Run bakeGrainCube + deriveGrain, the despun/shell route (an icy preset), and computeOcean/routeAndOrder with the same inputs before vs after the change; inspect that driversToTune reads the body-driver channel, not grainDrivers.
verifyVia.observable: Grain strike field byte-identical; despun/shell U byte-identical; ocean fraction + drainage stats (orphan/uphill counts, maxStrahler) unchanged; the plate tune is derived from a dedicated body-driver argument, and grainDrivers (despinAmp/radialStrainSign/radialStrainMag) is unmodified.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: LIVE driver-response probe: in the running lab on an Earth-like preset, sweeping a driver visibly changes the baked plate relief in the calibrated direction, an A/B of two driver draws at the same seed shows two distinct worlds, and the Earth preset stays byte-identical to a captured baseline.

verifyVia.input: Lab on :5173 (debug :9223), Rocky (Earthlike) preset, fix the seed, reliefBakeStrength(1), force a route; sweep gravity / volatiles / tidal-heating via the driver UI or a _lab driver override; call plateProbe(); capture A/B screenshots; then load the Earth reference preset and compare to baseline.
verifyVia.observable: heightSource=='carrier'; the probe shows the mapped parameter shifting in the calibrated direction as each driver is swept (plateCount / boundary-vs-latitude variance / continental area); the A/B at fixed seed reads as two visibly different worlds; the Earth reference preset's field matches the captured baseline.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: UAT (Max-only): two Earth-likes that differ only in their drivers read as genuinely different, recognizable, physically-sensible worlds (not the same world recolored), and the Earth preset still reads as the Earth Max already UAT-passed.

verifyVia.input: Max views, in the lab, the Earth reference preset (confirm unchanged) then several driver variants at a fixed seed: low-g vs high-g, dry vs ocean-rich, calm vs tidally-heated, young vs old.
verifyVia.observable: Max judges the variants as genuinely distinct + physically coherent worlds and Earth as unchanged; holistic acceptance. Never PASSed by any agent — deferred-to-max.

inputs: the per-body D-vector derived from DRIVER_PRESETS raw descriptors: D14 massGravity (from massEarth + radiusEarth), D2 volatileFraction (composition.volatileFraction, present), D12 tidalHeating (from eccentricity + orbitRadiusEarth + mass via the lab's star-tidal R^5/a^5 model)
plates.js DEFAULTS (the locked tunables) + the existing `tune` override seam (writePlateUpliftSphere(carrier, drivers, {macroSeed, tune}))

a named D_earth constant (the Earth reference point the calibration anchors to; note Earth maps to NON-zero normalized drivers, so transfer fns must return DEFAULTS at the real Earth values, not at a 0-vector)
macroSeed (integer); the lab's isEarthlikePlatePath gate (terrestrial/ocean, unlocked)
outputs: carrier.height via the driver-responsive plate tune (PLATE_COUNT_MIN/SPAN, UPLIFT_GAIN, CONTINENTAL_FRACTION now functions of (D-vector, macroSeed))
plateDiag (existing shape preserved; optionally the applied tune surfaced for the live plateProbe)
a new driversToTune(D) export in plates.js (pure, three-free)
mustStayWorking: the Earth reference point byte-identical to the validated plate POC (AC2 — the load-bearing identity guard)
the grain-cube bake byte-identical (AC5 — plate tune reads a NEW body-driver channel, NOT the grainDrivers bundle which the grain bake consumes)
the despun/ice-shell relief paths byte-identical (AC5 — shell regimes never see the plate tune)
plates.js DEFAULTS VALUES unchanged (this increment ADDS driversToTune + threading; it does not retune the locked defaults)
determinism: driversToTune is a pure function; no Math.random / Date.now; render-once (AC1)

filesTouched: EDIT src/worldengine/base/plates.js (add the D_earth constant + driversToTune(D) export + calibrated transfer functions; consume the drivers arg ONLY when producing a tune; remove the `void drivers` once consumed)

mustFix: #1 (BLOCKER, calibration — the ROADMAP increment-2 must-fix): define D_earth as a NAMED CONSTANT and calibrate every transfer function so f(D_earth) = DEFAULTS exactly; driversToTune(D_earth) returns null/empty so the ternary takes the untouched branch (AC2). The transfer-function shapes + signs must cite settled planetary-science scaling and be recorded in the build note (the per-driver direction AC3 asserts). Separate driver channel: add bodyDrivers (the D-vector) as a channel DISTINCT from grainDrivers (the grain-bake bundle) — do NOT repurpose grainDrivers (AC5 regression).
Scope guard: do NOT change plates.js DEFAULTS values; do NOT touch the despun/shell path, the grain bake internals, or game Planet.js.
